optional_suggestions: Hash comparison against the prior manifest. I compared all 50 source_files entries in attempt-03/input-manifest.json with attempt-02/input-manifest.json. The path set, modes and symlink flags are identical. Exactly 28 hashes differ: C01–C26, chunks/README.md, distribution.md and live-checks.md. They are the same 28 entries listed in delta.json. Each delta before_sha256 equals the attempt-02 manifest hash and each after_sha256 equals the attempt-03 manifest hash; I checked all 28 pairs. The other 22 hashes, including AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md, decisions.md, test-catalogue.md, review-protocol.md, dependencies.md and all prompts, are byte-identical. So other_source_changes=false is consistent with the manifests.

Checking the end-of-file state. I ran read-only multiline ripgrep across every *.md file. `
\z` matches every planning Markdown file, which confirms the anchor works. `

\z`, `\s\s\z` and `[^
]\z` match nothing, and there are no `` bytes under docs/planning. Every file therefore ends with exactly one LF and no trailing blank or whitespace-only line. This matches the stated after = before.rstrip(newline) + one newline.

Checking that nothing semantic changed. I re-read changed files at locations the attempt-02 verdict cited: C02.md milestones 5–6 and acceptance line 34; C24.md:11 and :31; C03.md milestones 4–5 and the T23 evidence clause; live-checks.md L01–L18, N01–N04 and F01–F09 with the required/not_required versus blocked-by-access separation; distribution.md's G01 manifest, its C26 precondition, Q24 still unselected and the informational-only Apache-2.0 note. All of them read as the prior review described. No planning requirement, decision, gate or prompt changed. Trailing LF bytes have no meaning in CommonMark rendering.

Make the normalization proof reproducible. delta.json says content_equal_after_eof_normalization is true but does not record how many LF bytes were removed from each file. Add removed_trailing_lf_count (k) per file. A third party could then confirm sha256(after_bytes + '\n'*k) == before_sha256 without the pre-edit bytes. Optionally, also record the git index or blob IDs used as the pre-edit source.

Add an explicit EOF-normalization assertion to checks.json, such as single_trailing_newline: true over the fingerprinted files. That way the formatting invariant is checked mechanically rather than only described in delta.json.
